Abstract: Herein, we report regiodivergent nucleophilic attack of Grignard reagents to 2-alkynyl aziridines.
Under the catalysis of a Cu(I)-diphosphine complex, benzylic Grignard reagents add to the carbon-carbon
triple bond of the aziridines to deliver α-allenylamines in moderate to excellent yields; the direct addition of
the Grignard reagents to the aziridines in the absence of catalyst provided homopropargylic amine derivatives.
Both reactions could proceed in highly enantiospecific ways. Further synthetic manipulations of these products
enable rapid access to diverse useful heterocyclic molecular scaffolds.
Keywords: aziridines; ring opening; Grignard reagents; alkynes; allenes

particular class of synthetic building blocks with multi-

Results and Discussion
We initiated the study by screening the reaction
conditions for the model reaction between aziridine 1 a
and the Grignard reagent 2 a (Table 1). After a prelimi-
nary screening of metal salts (see Table S1 in the SI for
details), [Cu(CH CN) ]PF was selected to evaluate
different phosphine ligands (entries 1–6). In general, the
presence of a phosphine ligand directed the reaction to
the formation of the allenic product 3 aa with high
selectivity and DPPF turned out to be the optimum
ligand (Table 1, entry 5). Notably, previous relevant
studies have been mainly restricted to aziridines bearing
a terminal alkyne moiety,<sup>[7–8]</sup> and the current study first
incorporates aziridines bearing an aryl alkyne into such
a transformation. Unfortunately, the use of several chiral
phosphine and BOX ligands hardly provided any chiral
induction in both the product and the recovered aziridine

Results and Discussion
We initiated the study by screening the reaction
conditions for the model reaction between aziridine 1 a
and the Grignard reagent 2 a (Table 1). After a prelimi-
nary screening of metal salts (see Table S1 in the SI for
details), [Cu(CH CN) ]PF was selected to evaluate
different phosphine ligands (entries 1–6). In general, the
presence of a phosphine ligand directed the reaction to
the formation of the allenic product 3 aa with high
selectivity and DPPF turned out to be the optimum
ligand (Table 1, entry 5). Notably, previous relevant
studies have been mainly restricted to aziridines bearing
a terminal alkyne moiety,<sup>[7–8]</sup> and the current study first
incorporates aziridines bearing an aryl alkyne into such
a transformation. Unfortunately, the use of several chiral
phosphine and BOX ligands hardly provided any chiral
induction in both the product and the recovered aziridine
(see Table S1 in the SI for details). An obvious solvent
effect on the reaction was also observed: the use of
toluene, MTBE and
\mathrm { E t } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }
as solvent all led to inferior
results in terms of both yield and product selectivity
(Table 1, entries 7–9). Decreasing the amount of either
the ligand or the catalyst combination or increasing the
reaction temperature led to inferior product selectivity
(Table 1, entries 10–12). In the absence of a ligand, the
S 2-type ring opening product 4aa was formed as
major product, which could be obtained almost quanti-
tatively when the reaction was performed in MTBE at
ambient temperature (Table 1, entry 16).

Next, the scope of the S 2-type ring opening reaction
of 2-alkynyl aziridines was investigated (Table 3). For
aziridines bearing aryl alkyne moieties, the reaction
proceeded smoothly to provide the desired homopropar-
gylic amine products in good to excellent yields (4 aa–

tuted alkynes provided allenic products (3ja and 3 ka)

alkyne was also not tolerated in this reaction to provide
the allenic product (3 la) in a low yield together with
unidentifiable complex mixture. The use of substituted
benzylic Grignard reagents generally provided moderate
yields in this reaction while the corresponding allenic
products and/or other unidentified side products were
formed concomitantly (4ab–4af). In addition, alkyl and
aryl Grignard reagents provided low yields of the
desired products (4 ag–4 ai) together with unidentifiable
complex mixture. It’s worth noting that in the presence
of the Cu(I)-dppf complex, the homopropargylic amine
products 4ah and 4ai were obtained in high yields
(Table 2). Vinyl (2j) and ethynyl (2k) Grignard reagents
